dedupe_keys.name: vancouver international airport yvr real time 3d digital twin built with unity

description: This case covers the real-time 3D digital twin of Vancouver International Airport (YVR), which the Vancouver Airport Authority built with the Unity engine and which Unity describes as the first of its kind at a North American airport, in a July 2023 case study. The twin is an interactive representation of the airfield and terminal connected to real-time operational data, and it combines historical and real-time data to support decisions on maintenance, sustainability and safety without disrupting operations. The airfield and terminal were captured with high-fidelity cameras and lidar on air and ground vehicles, existing CAD drawings were converted to Revit and imported into Unity, and a 3D modelling firm refined the model; the runtime is used by 200 operations staff and gives situational awareness to over 600 staff. Coverage is one airport in Richmond, British Columbia. Access: the case study is a free web page on Unity's website; the twin itself is internal and not published, so no licence applies. Outcome: the airport reports better resource planning from forecasting, faster root-cause analysis of disruptions and better situational awareness, and uses the twin to explore climate impact and security scenarios. Limitations: the account is a vendor case study without quantified results. The case is related to the Cologne/Bonn airport digital twin case catalogued here.
